name: NeuroForecast v3.1 interval study: coverage per culture batch
status: Fixed before any v3.1 interval was computed; the run records this file's SHA-256 in its output
question: The v3 study found batch-mean coverage on target (0.81 at nominal 0.80) but the worst fifth of batches at about 0.58. Can intervals that use each batch's day-5/day-7 information, or a two-level calibration, raise coverage in the worst batches without inflating width?
disclosure: Development comparison on the 41 batches of the v3 benchmark, using the locked v3 predictions of the v2 recipe (predictions/v2_incumbent.csv). Not a sealed test. The worst-fifth problem was seen in the v3 results before this protocol was written.
point_forecast: v2 recipe (v2_incumbent), its locked inner and outer predictions from the v3 run
folds: the v3 outer folds (9) and inner folds (4); every calibration quantity comes from the outer-training dates only
sigma: as in v3: Extra Trees on |inner out-of-fold residual| with the v2 sigma columns plus batch context, cross-fitted over the inner folds for calibration scores
batch_features: one row per batch, days 5 and 7 only: the 9 v3 batch-context descriptors, the 3 v2 batch covariates, and the batch medians of the plate-control reliability indicators

methods.pooled_scaled: v2 method: split-conformal quantile of |r|/sigma over calibration conditions
methods.batch_weighted: v3 method: the same scores weighted 1/(conditions on the batch)
methods.batch_adaptive: scores |r|/(sigma * b), where b is a batch difficulty predicted from the batch features by ridge regression (alpha 10, standardized) on log(median |r|/sigma) of calibration batches; b cross-fitted over inner folds for calibration scores; batch-weighted conformal quantile
methods.two_level: per calibration batch, the alpha-level quantile of |r|/sigma; the interval multiplier is the 0.8 conformal quantile of these per-batch quantiles, targeting at least nominal coverage in about 80% of batches

metrics: share of batches with coverage >= nominal - 0.1

success.batch_adaptive: batch-mean coverage within 0.77-0.83 at 0.80, worst-fifth coverage at 0.80 at least 0.05 above batch_weighted, and mean width at most 10% wider
success.two_level: reported as an assurance option: share of batches with coverage >= 0.70 at nominal 0.80, and the width it costs
